messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈0.01 MPa) the pressure is well below the triple‑point pressure of water (≈61 kPa). Under such low pressure water cannot exist as a stable liquid; the system will be either ice or vapor.  

If you’re interested in the **melting (freezing) temperature of ice** at that pressure, it’s roughly **–2 °C**. In other words, ice would melt (or water would freeze) at about –2 °C when the surrounding pressure is 10 kPa.  

Because the pressure is below the triple point, the concept of a “freezing point” for liquid water isn’t strictly applicable—there simply isn’t a liquid phase under those conditions.
